62:1: God Almighty says: Everything in the seven heavens and everything on the earth of His creation glorifies God and magnifies Him willingly or unwillingly, the Holy King to whom belongs the kingdom of this world and the Hereafter and their authority, whose command is effective in the heavens and the earth and everything in them, the Holy: He is pure from everything that the polytheists attribute to Him and describe Him with that is not from His attributes, the Blessed, the Mighty meaning the severe in His vengeance upon His enemies, the Wise in His management of His creation and His disposition of them in what He knows best of their interests.
62:2: God Almighty says: God is He who sent among the unlettered a Messenger from among themselves. His statement is a metaphor for the name of God, and the unlettered are the Arabs. We have previously explained the meaning for which the unlettered person is called ummi. And in a similar manner to what we said about the illiterate in this place, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: It is He who sent among the unlettered a Messenger from among themselves. He said: The Arabs. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: I heard Sufyan al-Thawri narrating, and I do not know of it except on the authority of Mujahid, that he said: It is He who sent among the unlettered a Messenger from themselves reciting to them His verses: the Arabs. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, It is He who sent among the unlettered a Messenger from among themselves. He said: This tribe of Arabs was an illiterate nation, with no book that they could read, so God sent His Prophet Muhammad as a mercy and guidance to guide them with. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, It is He who sent among the unlettered a Messenger from among themselves. He said: This nation was illiterate and did not read a book. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, It is He who has sent among the unlettered a Messenger from themselves, he said: The nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was called the unlettered because no book was sent down to them. And God Almighty said, a Messenger from them, meaning from the unlettered. And He only said from them because Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was unlettered, and he appeared from the Arabs. And His statement: He recites to them His verses, meaning that He, the Most High, says: He recites to these illiterate people the verses of God that He sent down to him. And purifies them, meaning: He cleanses them from the filth of disbelief. His statement, And He teaches them the Book, means: He teaches them the Book of God, and what it contains of God’s commands and prohibitions, and the laws of His religion. And wisdom, meaning by wisdom: the Sunnahs. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And He teaches them the Book and wisdom, meaning the Sunnah. Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, he said: And He purifies them and teaches them the Book and wisdom also, just as He taught these, He purifies them with the Book and righteous deeds, and He teaches them the Book and wisdom as He did with the former ones. And he recited the words of God Almighty: And the first forerunners among the Muhajireen and the Ansar and those who followed them with good conduct (al-Tawbah 9:100), from among the people of Islam until the Hour comes. He said: And God has made forerunners among them. And he recited the words of God Almighty: And the first forerunners - those are the ones brought near (al-Waqi’ah 56:10), and he said: A group of the former and a few of the latter (al-Waqi’ah 56:13), so a group of the former are forerunners, and a few are forerunners, and a few are forerunners among the latter ones. And he recited: And the companions of the right hand - what are the companions of the right hand? (al-Waqi’ah 56:27), until he reached: A group of the former and a group of the latter ones (al-Waqi’ah 56:39). He also said: And the forerunners among the former ones are more and the latter ones are few. And he recited: And those who They came after them saying, “Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith. (al-Hashr 59:10) He said: These are from the people of Islam until the Hour comes. And His statement, And they were before in manifest error, God Almighty says: And these unlettered people were, before God sent among them a Messenger from among them, in transgression against the straight path, and taking without clear guidance. He says: It becomes clear to whoever contemplates it that they were in transgression and transgression against the truth and the path of right guidance.
62:3: God Almighty says: And it is He who sent among the unlettered a Messenger from among themselves, and among others from among them who have not yet joined them. So, others is in the accusative case in apposition to the unlettered. There is a difference of opinion about those meant by his saying and others among them. Some of them said: He meant the Persians. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told me, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And others among them who have not yet joined them, he said: They are the non-Arabs. Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told us: Fadil bin Talha told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And others among them who have not yet joined them, he said: They are the non-Arabs. Abu Al-Sa’ib told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, And others of them who have not yet joined them, he said: The non-Arabs. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Asim told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, And others of them who have not yet joined them [He said: The non-Arabs. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: I heard Sufyan al-Thawri, I do not know it except on the authority of Mujahid: And others of them who have not yet joined them. He said: The non-Arabs. Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me: Yahya ibn Ma’in told us: Hisham ibn Yusuf told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Umar ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-As, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that he said to him: Surat al-Jumu’ah was revealed about us and you regarding your killing of the Liar. Then he recited, Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God, until he reached, and others among them who have not yet joined them. He said: So you are they. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, And others of them who have not yet joined them, he said: The non-Arabs. Muhammad ibn Muammar told me, he said: Abu Amir told us, he said: Abdul Aziz told us, and Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Sulayman ibn Bilal told me, all of them, on the authority of Thawr ibn Zayd, on the authority of Abu al-Ghaith, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: We were sitting with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when Surat al-Jumu’ah was revealed to him. When he recited, And others among them who have not yet joined them, a man said, Who are these, O Messenger of God? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not respond to him until he had asked him once, twice, or three times. He said, And among us is Salman al-Farsi. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, placed his hand on Salman and said, If faith were at the Pleiades, men from these would attain it. Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman told me, he said: My uncle told us, he said: Sulayman bin Bilal Al-Madani told us, on the authority of Thawr bin Zayd, on the authority of Salim Abu Al-Ghaith, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: We were sitting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar. Others said: What is meant by this is all those who entered Islam after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, whoever they may be, until the Day of Resurrection. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, And others of them who have not yet joined them, he said: From among all people who embraced Islam. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of God Almighty, And others of them who have not yet joined them, he said: These are everyone who came after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, until the Day of Resurrection, everyone who entered Islam from the Arabs and the non-Arabs. The more correct of the two opinions in this regard, in my opinion, is the opinion of the one who said: What is meant by this is every person who came after those who accompanied the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their Islam, from any race, because God Almighty made his statement, and others among them who have not yet joined them, general in meaning every person who came after them from among the others, and He did not specify one type among them over another. So every person who came after them is from the others who were not counted among the first to whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited God’s verses. His saying: When they have not yet joined them means: They have not yet come, but they will come. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement, when they have not yet joined them, he said: they have not yet come. And His saying, And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise, means: And God is the Exalted in His vengeance against those who disbelieve in Him among them, and the Wise in His management of His creation.
62:4: And His statement: That is the bounty of God which He gives to whom He wills. God Almighty says: This which God Almighty did by sending among the illiterate Arabs and others a Messenger from among them who recites to them His verses and does all that He described, is God's bounty, which He bestowed upon these people and not upon others. That He gives to whom He wills. He says: He gives that bounty of His to whom He wills from among His creation. He does not deserve blame from the one whom God has deprived of it, because He did not prevent him from a right that he had before, nor did He wrong him by diverting it from him to someone else. Rather, He knew who had a bounty, so He entrusted it to him and placed it with him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz told us: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, on the authority of Shabib, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding That is the bounty of God which He bestows upon whom He wills, he said: Bounty is religion. And God is the possessor of great bounty, he says: God is the possessor of bounty upon His servants, the good among them and the bad, and those among whom He sent the Messenger and others, the Great One before whom the bounty of every one with bounty is little.
62:5: God Almighty says: The example of those who were given the Torah from among the Jews and Christians, and they carried out the work according to it, then they did not carry it meaning: then they did not act according to what was in it, and they denied Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, even though they were commanded to believe in him in it, follow him, and confirm him, is like the example of a donkey carrying volumes meaning: like the example of a donkey carrying books of knowledge on its back, but it does not benefit from them, nor does it understand what is in them. Likewise, those who were given the Torah, which contains an explanation of the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, are like the example of a donkey who carries books containing knowledge, but it does not understand them or benefit from them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, carrying books, he said: He carries books but does not know what is in them, nor does he understand them. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not uphold it is like that of a donkey who carries volumes. He said: It carries a book and does not know what is on it, nor what is in it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Like a donkey carrying books, he said: Like a donkey carrying books, not knowing what is on its back. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Like a donkey carrying volumes, “books,” and the book in Nabataean is called a book. God set forth this as an example for those who were given the Torah and then disbelieved. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not uphold it is like that of a donkey who carries volumes. The volumes are the books. So God made the example of the one who reads a book but does not follow what is in it like the example of a donkey who carries the heavy Book of God, not knowing what is in it. Then He said, Evil is the example of the people who deny the verses of God. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding the statement of God, Like a donkey carrying volumes, he said: The volumes are the Torah, which the donkey carries on its back, just as the copies of the Qur’an are carried on beasts of burden, like a man who travels and carries his Qur’an. He said: So the donkey does not benefit from it when he carries it on his back. Likewise, these people did not benefit from it when they did not act upon it, even though they were given it, just as this one did not benefit from it while it was on his back. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Like a donkey carrying volumes, he said: Books, and volumes is the plural of safar, and they are large books. And His statement: How evil is the example of the people who deny the signs of God. He says: How evil is this example, the example of the people who deny the signs of God, meaning His proofs and arguments. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people. God Almighty says: And God does not guide the people who wronged themselves, so they disbelieved in the signs of their Lord.
62:6: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to the Jews, Say, O you who are Jews, if you claim that you are allies of God to the exclusion of people, then wish for death, if you should be truthful, in your claim that you are allies of God to the exclusion of people, for God does not punish His allies, rather He honors them and bestows blessings upon them. And if you are truthful in what you say, then wish for death so that you may be relieved of the distress, worries, and sorrows of this world, and so that you may reach the spirit of Paradise and its bliss through death. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Say, ‘O you who are Jews,’ “Say, ‘O you who have repented,’” referring to the Jews. Moses said, Indeed, we have been guided to You (al-A’raf 7:156), Indeed, we have repented to You.
62:7: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, And they will never wish for it. He says: The Jews will never wish for death. Because of what their hands have put forth. Meaning: Because of the sins they have acquired in this world and the evil deeds they have committed. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers. He says: God is All-Knowing of those among His creation who have wronged themselves, destroying themselves by their disbelief in God.
62:8: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say O Muhammad to the Jews: Indeed, the death from which you flee “and you hate it, and you refuse to wish for it” it will meet you “and descend upon you” then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed “then your Lord will return you after your death to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Knower of the unseen of the heavens and the earth” and the witnessed means what is witnessed and appears to the eye, and is not hidden from the sight of the observers. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Qatada recited: Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and he said: God humiliated Adam with death, and I do not know anything about it except that He raised him up. Then He will inform you of what you used to do, meaning: Then He will inform you of the deeds you used to do in this world, both the bad and the good, because He encompasses all of them. Then He will reward you for that: the doer of good for his good, and the doer of evil for what he deserves.
62:9: God Almighty says to His believing servants: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, When the call is made for the prayer on Friday, and that is the call, calling to the Friday prayer when the imam sits on the pulpit to deliver the sermon. The meaning of the words: When the call is made for the prayer on Friday, then hasten to the remembrance of God, meaning: So proceed to the remembrance of God and work for Him. The root of striving in this context is work, and we have already mentioned the evidence for that previously. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Ismail bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Shurahbil bin Muslim Al-Khawlani, regarding the statement of God, So hasten to the remembrance of God, he said: So hasten in action, and hastening is not walking. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, O you who have believed, when the call is made for the prayer on the day of Jumu’ah [Friday], then proceed to the remembrance of God. And striving, O son of Adam, is to strive with your heart and your actions, which is to proceed to it. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, who said: Mughirah told me, on the authority of Ibrahim, that it was said to Umar, may God be pleased with him: Ubayy recites it as Fas’u. He said: He is the most knowledgeable of us about the abrogated verses, and it is only Famudi. Abdul Hamid bin Bayan Al-Sakari told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of his father, who said: I never heard Omar recite it except that he proceeded. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Yaman told us, he said: Hanthala told us, on the authority of Salim bin Abdullah, he said: Omar, may God be pleased with him, used to recite it Then proceed to the remembrance of God. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hanthala, on the authority of Salim ibn Abdullah, that Umar ibn al-Khattab recited it: Then proceed. Yunus bin Abdul-A’la told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Hanzala bin Abi Sufyan Al-Jumahi told us, that he heard Salim bin Abdullah narrating on the authority of his father, that he heard Umar bin Al-Khattab recite When the call to prayer is made on Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of God. He said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said: Salim bin Abdullah bin Omar told me, that Abdullah said: God took Omar, may God be pleased with him, and he did not recite this verse in which God mentioned al-Jumuah 62:O you who have believed, when the call is made for the prayer on the day of Friday except proceed to the remembrance of God. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Abdullah used to recite it So proceed to the remembrance of God, and he would say: If you had recited it, then hasten, I would have hastened until my cloak fell off. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Salman, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Abdullah said: If the sa’i was to be performed, I would have sa’i until my cloak fell off. He said: But it is so proceed to the remembrance of God. He said: This is how he used to recite it. Ali bin Al-Hussein Al-Azdi told me: Yahya bin Yaman Al-Azdi told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar Al-Razi, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah, that he used to recite it So proceed to the remembrance of God. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Yaman told us, he said: Abu Ja`far told us, on the authority of al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah, that he recited it Then proceed to the remembrance of God. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, who said: It is for the free. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Masruq, who said: At the time. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Masruq: When the call to prayer is made, he said: At the time. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: It is when making a decision, when giving a sermon, when making remembrance. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, When the call is made for prayer on Friday, he said: The call at the time of remembrance is an obligation. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, When the call to prayer is made on Friday, he said: The intention is to remember God during the sermon. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Mughira and Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: If I had read it Fas’a, I would have walked until my cloak fell off. And he used to read it Famdim ila remembrance of God. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: He recited it so proceed. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Hayyan, on the authority of Ikrimah: So strive to the remembrance of God. He said: Striving means action. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, and I asked him about the statement of God, When the call is made for the prayer on the day of Jumu’ah, then hasten to the remembrance of God, he said: When you hear the first caller, respond to it and hasten and do not delay. He said: There were no calls to prayer during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, except two calls to prayer: the call to prayer when he sits on the pulpit, and the call to prayer when the prayer is established. He said: This second call to prayer is something that the people introduced later. He said: It is not permissible for him to sell if he hears the call that is made before the imam when he sits on the pulpit and recites, So hasten to the remembrance of God and leave off trading. He said: He did not command them to leave off anything else. He forbade trading, then permitted it for them when they finished the prayer. He said: Hastening means to hasten to it, to go to it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: In the wording of Ibn Mas’ud it says: When the call to prayer is made on Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of God. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, So strive towards the remembrance of God, striving is action. God said, Indeed, your striving is diverse (al-Layl 92:4). His saying: And leave off buying and selling means: Leave off buying and selling when the call to prayer is made during the sermon. Al-Dahhak used to say about this: Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: When the sun has set, buying and selling is forbidden. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: When the call to prayer is made on Friday, he said: When the sun has passed its zenith, buying and selling is forbidden. Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, who said: There were people sitting in Baqi’ al-Zubayr, buying and selling when the call to prayer was made on Friday, and they did not get up. So the verse When the call to prayer is made on Friday was revealed. As for the remembrance that God Almighty commanded His believing servants to strive for, it is the imam’s admonition in his sermon regarding what was said. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, When the call to prayer is made on Friday, he said: The intention is to remember God during the sermon. Abdullah bin Muhammad al-Hanafi told us: Abdun told us: Abdullah told us: Mansur, a man from the people of Kufa, told us, on the authority of Musa bin Abi Katheer, that he heard Saeed bin al-Musayyab say: When the call to prayer is made on Friday, hasten to remember God. He said: It is the imam’s sermon, and when the prayer is completed after that. His saying, That is better for you, if you only knew, means: Your striving when the call to prayer is made on Friday, when God is mentioned, and refraining from buying and selling at that time is better for you than buying and selling at that time, if you know the benefits and harms of yourselves. The reciters differed in their recitation of the phrase on Friday. The majority of the reciters in the regions recited it as Friday with a damma on the meem and the jim, except for Al-A’mash, who recited it with a soft meem. The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is what is read in the regions, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.
62:10: God Almighty says: So when the Friday prayer is over on Friday, then disperse throughout the land if you wish. This is a concession from God to you in that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mujahid, that he said: It is a concession, meaning his statement: So when the prayer has been concluded, disperse throughout the land. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land, that this is permission from God, so whoever wishes may go out, and whoever wishes may sit. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, God gave them permission when they finished the prayer, So when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of God, for He has made it lawful for you. And his saying, And seek from the bounty of God, was mentioned from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the interpretation of that: Al-Abbas ibn Abi Talib told me: Ali ibn al-Mu'afa ibn Ya'qub al-Mawsili told us: Abu Amir al-Sa'igh from Mosul told us, on the authority of Abu Khalaf, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding His statement, So when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of God, that he said: Not to seek this world, but to visit the sick, attend a funeral, and visit a brother in God. His saying, And seek from the bounty of God, may possibly mean: And seek from the bounty of God, in whose hand are the keys to His treasuries for your world and your hereafter. And His statement, And remember God often that you may succeed, means: Remember God by praising Him and thanking Him for the blessings He has bestowed upon you in terms of enabling you to perform His duties, so that you may succeed, attain your requests from your Lord, and attain eternal life in His Paradise.
62:11: God Almighty says: And when the believers see a caravan of trade or amusement, they rush to it meaning they hasten to the trade and leave you standing He says to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And they leave you, O Muhammad, standing on the pulpit. That is because the trade that they saw, and the people rushed to it and left the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, standing, was oil that Dihya bin Khalifah had brought from Syria. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, who said: Dihya ibn Khalifah came with an oil trade from Syria, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the Friday sermon. When they saw him, they stood up to him in al-Baqi’, fearing that they would be beaten to it. He said: Then the verse was revealed: And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse to it and leave you standing. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Yaman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Qurrah, When the call to prayer is made on Friday, he said: Dihya Al-Kalbi came with merchandise while the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was standing in prayer on Friday, so they left the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and went out to him, so the verse was revealed, And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse to it and leave you standing, until he finished the surah. Abu Hasin Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Yunus told me, he said: Abthar told us, he said: Hasin told us, on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Ja`d, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on Friday, and a caravan carrying food passed by. He said: So the people went out except for twelve men, and the verse about Friday was revealed. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Al-Hasan said: The people of Medina were afflicted with hunger and high prices. A caravan came while the Prophet was delivering the Friday sermon, and they heard about it, so they went out while the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was standing, as God Almighty said. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse to it and leave you standing, he said: A transaction came and they dispersed to it, and left the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, standing. And when they see amusement and play, “Say, ‘What is with God is better than amusement and amusement. And God is the best of providers.’” Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And when they see a trade or amusement, they disperse to it, he said: Men who used to go to their camels and to travel, seeking trade. “Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the sermon to the people on Friday, they kept slipping away and standing until a group remained. He said: How many are you? So they counted themselves and there were twelve men and women. Then he stood up on the second Friday and began to deliver the sermon to them. Sufyan said: I do not know except that it is in his hadith, admonishing them and reminding them. So they kept slipping away and standing until a group remained. He said: How many are you? So they counted themselves and there were twelve men and women. Then he stood up on the third Friday and they kept slipping away and standing until a group remained. He said: How many are you? So they counted themselves and there were twelve men and women. He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if the last of you were to follow the first of you, the valley would burn you in fire. And God, the Almighty, revealed: ‘And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse to it and leave you standing.’” Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, They dispersed towards it and left you standing, he said: If the last of them had followed the first of them, the valley would have been engulfed in fire upon them. He said: Ibn Thaur told us, Muammar said, Qatada said: There remained with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on that day only twelve men and a woman with them. Muhammad ibn Amara al-Razi told us: Muhammad ibn al-Sabah told us: Hisham told us: Hisin told us, on the authority of Salim and Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, regarding his statement, and they left you standing, he said: A caravan came and they dispersed to it, and there remained with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, only twelve men. Amr bin Abdul Hamid Al-Amli narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Jabir, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the sermon while standing on Friday, when a caravan came from Ash-Sham, and the people turned to it until only twelve men remained. He said: This verse was revealed regarding al-Jumuah 62:And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse to it and leave you standing. As for amusement, there is a difference of opinion as to which type of amusement it was. Some of them said: It was arrogance and musical instruments. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar told us, he said: Yahya ibn Salih told us, he said: Sulayman ibn Bilal told us, on the authority of Ja`far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Jabir ibn `Abdullah, he said: When the slave girls were married, they would pass by the music and flutes and leave the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, standing on the pulpit, and they would disperse to them. Then God revealed: And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse to it. Others said: It was a drum. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Al-Haww: the drum. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Ashib told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, he said: Abdullah bin Abi Nujayh mentioned, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Abi Bakr, on the authority of Mujahid, that Al-Lahu is the drum. What is more correct in this story is what we narrated on the authority of Jabir, because he had witnessed the affairs of the people and their scenes. And His saying, Say, ‘What is with God is better than amusement and trade.’ God Almighty is saying to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Say to them, O Muhammad, that which is with God of reward, for whoever sits listening to the sermon and exhortation of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, on Friday until the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, finishes it, is better for him than amusement and trade to which they disperse. And God is the Best of Providers. He says: And God is the Best Provider, so turn to Him in seeking your provisions, and ask Him to expand upon you from His bounty, not from anyone else.
